results.title: Monotone energy stability of magnetohydrodynamics Couette and Hartmann flows
results.theorem:
Assuming that the Reynolds number satisfies condition



${\rm Re\,}<{\rm Re}_{E},$



the basic magnetic Couette and Hartmann motions are monotone asympotically stable in the energy norm $E$ according to the inequality



$E(t)\leq E(0)e^{\frac{\pi^{2}}{2}c_{0}({\rm Re\,}-{\rm Re}_{E})t},$



with a positive constant $c_{0}$ depending on ${\rm Ha}$ and ${\rm Pm}$.

results.title: Rigorous derivation of the Fick cross-diffusion system from the multi-species Boltzmann equation in the diffusive scaling
results.theorem:
Let $\mathbf{n^{\varepsilon}}(t,x)=\mathbf{n_{\infty}}+\mathbf{\widetilde{n}}(t,x)$ be a perturbative solution of the Fick system (constructed in Theorem 2.3), which defines the Maxwellian $\mathbf{M}^{\varepsilon}(t,x,v)=\mathbf{n^{\varepsilon}}(t,x)\boldsymbol{\mu}(v)$. Assume $(H1)-(H2)-(H3)-(H4)$ are satisfied on the collision kernel and that $s>d/2$.
There exist real numbers $\delta_{\rm fluid},\>\delta_{B}>0$ such that, if the initial datum $\mathbf{F^{(\mbox{\footnotesize in})}}$ satisfies


(i)

$\left\|\mathbf{\widetilde{n}^{\rm(in)}}\right\|_{H^{s+2}_{x}}\leqslant\delta_{\rm fluid}$,



(ii)

$\displaystyle{\mathbf{f^{(\mbox{\footnotesize{in}})}}}\in\mathcal{H}^{s}_{\varepsilon}$ with $\left\|\mathbf{f^{(\mbox{\footnotesize{in}})}}\right\|_{\mathcal{H}^{s}_{\varepsilon}}\leqslant\delta_{B}$ and $\displaystyle{\left|\int_{\mathbb{T}^{d}}\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathbf{L}}(\mathbf{f^{(\mbox{\footnotesize{in}})}})dx\right|\leqslant\delta_{\mbox{\footnotesize{fluid}}}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathbf{L}}$ is the orthogonal projection in $L^{2}_{v}(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{-1/2})$ onto $\mathop{\mathrm{Ker}}(\mathbf{L})$ (see Subsection 3.1),



then the multispecies Boltzmann equation (1.1) possesses a unique global perturbative solution $\mathbf{F^{\varepsilon}}(t,x,v)=\mathbf{M}^{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}}(t,x)+\varepsilon\mathbf{f^{\varepsilon}}(t,x,v)\geqslant 0$, with $\mathbf{f^{\varepsilon}}\in C^{0}\left(\mathbb{R}^{+};H^{s}_{x,v}\left(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{-1/2}\right)\right)$.
Moreover, there exists a constant $C_{B}>0$ and a norm ∥⋅∥ℋεs\left\|\cdot\right\|_{\mathcal{H}^{s}_{\varepsilon}}, equivalent to the following weighted hypocoercive norm



∥⋅∥ℋεs2∼∥⋅∥Lx,v2​(𝝁−1/2)2+∑|α|⩽s∥∂xα⋅∥Lx,v2​(𝝁−1/2)2+ε2∑|α|+|β|⩽s|β|⩾1∥∂vβ∂xα⋅∥Lx,v2​(𝝁−1/2)2,\left\|\cdot\right\|_{\mathcal{H}^{s}_{\varepsilon}}^{2}\sim\left\|\cdot\right\|_{L^{2}_{x,v}\left(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{-1/2}\right)}^{2}+\sum_{|\alpha|\leqslant s}\left\|\partial^{\alpha}_{x}\cdot\right\|_{L^{2}_{x,v}\left(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{-1/2}\right)}^{2}+\varepsilon^{2}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}|\alpha|+|\beta|\leqslant s\\[0.56905pt]
|\beta|\geqslant 1\end{subarray}}\left\|\partial^{\beta}_{v}\partial^{\alpha}_{x}\cdot\right\|_{L^{2}_{x,v}\left(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{-1/2}\right)}^{2},



such that the solution to the Boltzmann equation (1.1) satisfies the following stability property for all $t\geqslant 0$



$\left\|\mathbf{F^{\varepsilon}}-\mathbf{M}^{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}}\right\|_{\mathcal{H}^{s}_{\varepsilon}}(t)\leqslant\varepsilon C_{B}.$



All the constant are explicit and independent of $\varepsilon$.

(2.1)

problem (1.4)–(1.6) in the following sense:


(1)

If $|m|<m_{\mathrm{C}}^{{i}}$, then the equilibrium state $(\bar{\rho},0,\bar{M})$ of the problem (1.4)–(1.6)

$\mathcal{E}_{\sigma}(w,\Lambda):=\int g\bar{\rho}^{\prime}w_{3}^{2}\mathrm{d}x-\lambda_{0}m^{2}\int|\partial_{i}w|^{2}\mathrm{d}x-\Lambda\mu\int|\nabla w|^{2}\mathrm{d}x.$
